title: Cloudflare-hosted Composer execution
question: What can the deployed App Composer Worker actually run today, which bindings does it really have, and which model ids, if any, is it able to execute?

entries.label: Deployed Worker identity
entries.observed: build.json returns commit 8d5d0c50390cdd64df48b3040758f6398087fb0e with sourceCommittedAt 2026-11-16T10:15:31+11:00 and contract 1. The newest deployment is aec9073c-81af-4f0c-a06d-f0fdb5486d75, created 2026-11-15T23:17:05.807105Z, serving version 2b418c92-7620-4779-b992-c2c10dcc7d67. origin/main is three commits ahead of the deployed commit.
entries.note: This inventory describes the deployed commit, not main.

entries.label: Model-inference binding
entries.observed: HTTP 200. The binding list contains assets, plain_text, secret_text, service, d1, r2_bucket, kv_namespace and ratelimit entries, and no binding of type ai, inference, vectorize, browser or hyperdrive.
entries.note: There is no Workers AI binding on the deployed Worker, so it cannot execute any @cf model itself. This is the finding, not a temporary outage.

entries.label: Model ids the Worker can execute
entries.source: grep for env.AI, run("@cf and provider origins across src/; the same settings response
entries.observed: Zero. Composer's source contains no Workers AI call, no ai binding access and no request to a model provider origin. The only @cf string in the application is an example command printed in the media admin UI (src/plugins/media-admin.tsx:695), addressed to the independent Studio agent.
entries.note: A benchmark row labelled "Cloudflare-hosted Composer" has nothing to execute in this runtime today.

entries.label: DB · D1
entries.observed: One d1 binding named DB on database 1b2b29c8-4109-4a5f-901a-befc91173bc5 (app-composer-emdash).
entries.note: Stores application and workspace records, not media.

entries.label: MEDIA · R2
entries.observed: One r2_bucket binding named MEDIA on bucket app-composer-media.
entries.note: Bytes only. No model is reachable through this binding.

entries.label: USAGE_LIMIT · rate limit
entries.note: Bounds request rate. It does not meter model spend, because no model runs here.

entries.label: Five service bindings
entries.observed: service bindings GUESTBOOK and SHOWCASE and GUESTBOOK_MEMBERS on composer-guestbook-8428e16f61c25a4d and composer-showcase-8428e16f61c25a4d, plus CREATOR_HUB_GUESTBOOK on creator-hub-guestbook and CREATOR_HUB_SHOWCASE on creator-hub-showcase.
entries.note: Independent mini-apps reached in-process. None of them is a model runtime, and no Studio binding exists.

entries.label: Secret names present
entries.observed: Secrets are present by name only and no value was read: CF_ACCESS_AUDIENCE, COMPOSER_PROFILE_BRIDGE_TOKEN, EMDASH_ENCRYPTION_KEY, GUESTBOOK_MEMBER_TOKEN, GUESTBOOK_OWNER_TOKEN, MEDIA_AGENT_TOKEN, MEDIA_STUDIO_BRIDGE_SECRET, MEDIA_STUDIO_ORIGIN, OWNER_API_TOKEN, OYSTER_MEDIA_INSTALLATION, OYSTER_ORIGIN, OYSTER_OWNER_KEY, RESEND_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS, RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS, USAGE_TOKENS, WOODHOUSE_GITHUB_TOKEN.
entries.note: Recorded so a reader can see which delegated capabilities exist without any credential being exposed.

entries.label: Delegated media generation
entries.source: src/lib/media-capability-runtime.mjs (readModels, refreshCatalogue, submitGeneration); the secret names above
entries.observed: The Worker can read a connected media host's model catalogue into media_workspace_connections and submit a generation to that host over HTTP, using the MEDIA_STUDIO_ORIGIN / MEDIA_STUDIO_BRIDGE_SECRET or an OYSTER credential reference. The model ids come from the connected host at runtime, never from Composer's code.
entries.note: So Composer can cause execution elsewhere and record the result. It does not execute the model, and the ids are the host's, listed in the Studio inventory.

entries.label: Per-workspace connection state
entries.observed: media_workspace_connections holds which workspace is connected to which host. Reading it would read customer workspace data, which this check did not do.
entries.reason: Whether any live workspace has an enabled media connection is production customer data. It was deliberately not queried, so no connection is claimed to be active.
entries.note: The capability is verified in code; its per-workspace enablement is not asserted.

entries.label: Account Workers AI eligibility
entries.observed: HTTP 403, error code 10000 "Authentication error". The token on this machine can read Worker settings, deployments and routes but not the Workers AI model catalogue.
entries.reason: The account-level Workers AI catalogue and per-model eligibility could not be read with the available credential. Composer has no Workers AI binding anyway, so this limits the Studio's evidence, not Composer's.
entries.note: No model id is marked eligible for this account on the strength of the account alone.

sources.shape: 200 JSON: app, commit, reviewed, sourceCommittedAt, contract
200 JSON: result.bindings[] with type and name; result.compatibility_date 2026-10-13; compatibility_flags nodejs_compat, global_fetch_strictly_public
200 JSON: ten deployments, each with id, created_on, source "wrangler", versions[].version_id
403 JSON: success false, errors[0].code 10000, message "Authentication error"

limits: This is the first recorded check for this plane, so there is no previous value to diff. The changes list is empty by fact, not by omission.
The inventory describes deployed commit 8d5d0c5. Three commits on origin/main are not deployed, so a later release invalidates the deployment row and nothing else here without a fresh read.
Secret values were never read. Only the binding names and types from the Worker's own settings response are recorded.
Whether a workspace has an enabled media connection is customer data and was not queried.
Account-level Workers AI eligibility is unverified because the available token is refused by that endpoint; no eligibility claim is made for any model id.
